old: The better order is less cinematic, more like this: practice together, process a real conflict, clarify your values, test membership, decide ownership and exit, and only then think about land.
new: The better order is less cinematic: 1) practice together, 2) process a real conflict, 3) clarify your values, 4) test membership, 5) decide ownership and exit, and 6) only then think about land.

old: Remote or constrained readers can build the portion available. Hold a weekly meal with two households. Arrange a counseling exchange with one friend in person or by video. Share tools and childcare, or transport and food preparation. Or a sauna! Add acro-yoga, dance improvisation, a mothers' circle, or a [cuddle puddle](http://cuddleparty.com/) if you're hippie enough.
new: Here's an idea if you're remote, or stuck where you are: build the part of it you actually can. Have a weekly meal with two households. Set up a counseling exchange with one friend, in person or by video. Share tools and childcare, or transport and food prep. Or a sauna! And if you're hippie enough, add acro-yoga, dance improv, a mothers' circle or a [cuddle puddle](http://cuddleparty.com/).

old: Where can you find them? Maybe at an unprogrammed Quaker meeting, or a restorative-practice group. Open-hearted congregations, mature recovery groups and meditation groups are worth a try too. And look for the people who came back from a long retreat kinder, rather than more impressed with themselves!
